abilities.costs: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
abilities.effects: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

reviews.reason: Eating already handles intake, but no implemented capability prepares food for later consumption. A minimal feasible preparation is crushing safe roots using an acquired stone and bark work surface. It requires no assumed fire, equipment or new food stock. Preparation preserves nutrition rather than creating additional nutrition or detoxification. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: Crushing alone does not earn wellbeing, and there is no established physical reason for a nutrition bonus. Actual eating can provide bounded enjoyment of a substantial safe meal, including repeated enjoyment. Bind one canonical food-enjoyment rule to meal-experience, shared with raw and preserved food rather than a preparation-specific alias: participant is the actual eater; require at least 8 nutrition actually accepted within the existing 10-round meal window, nonspoiled nontoxic food, and a positive appetite at intake. Award 0.4 transient pleasure, source cap 0.8, duration 4 rounds, refresh rather than stack, cooldown 10 rounds per eater across all food forms. Emit at most once for the same intake window; no reward for discarded overflow or processing. This finite meal does not establish a maintained satisfaction source. A separately performed qualifying experiment may use the existing information-confirmed rule through probe, never an automatic reward for completing preparation.
reviews.visualReview: Show the real stone, bark surface and reserved roots at the work location, followed by a visibly crushed food stack only after completion. Display remaining work, paid energy, original ingredients, nutrition, spoilage and the absence of cooking or preservation. Replay paid crushing steps and completion/cancellation using the declared process events; no meal, warmth or wellbeing animation occurs merely on registration or learning.
reviews.specification: Implement root-preparation-v1. Public schema: {operation:'prepare', inputStackId, quantity, stoneId, barkId, processId?}; use shared actor/item/object/process references, world coordinates, mass units and simulation rounds. Require living actor, individual mastery, positive integral quantity, owned unspoiled meadow roots, an actual owned stone unit and bark unit, and placement on accessible, unoccupied ground within 0.65 interaction distance. Stone and bark are reusable implements, unavailable for simultaneous conflicting operations; acquire them separately. No fire or water is required. Record input identities, quantity, accumulated spoilage, composition, harvest history, tool references, owner, location, remaining work and paid energy. Perform two active rounds per root at 1 energy per round, including setup and crushing. Reserve roots in uniquely owned process escrow; continue their actual decay. Each paid round reduces remaining work exactly once. Pause on movement out of reach or insufficient energy. Completion atomically converts escrow into crushed-root food owned by the actor; conserve edible mass, 14 nutrition per input root, zero initial toxicity, and original provenance. No washing, sterilization or extended shelf life is implied; crushed food decays at 1.25 times its corresponding unprocessed rate and never resets accumulated spoilage. Existing eat must accept this composition and apply normal satiety, toxicity and spoilage rules, without direct healing. Cancellation, including death, releases the actual unfinished crushed/raw mixture at the process location with its current composition and decay; spent effort is not refunded, and escrow is neither duplicated nor deleted. Tools remain actual world items. The work patch is a non-solid radius-0.3 ground footprint, cannot overlap incompatible occupied work surfaces, and creates no room, shade or collision barrier. Declare food-preparation-started and food-preparation-completed; bind paid updates and cancellation to process-progress, process-completed and process-stopped. Dependencies are item reservation, composite edible state, existing decay/eat and shared geometry; implement these in this handoff. Migrate existing stacks unchanged; add processing history only to transformed portions. Keep implementation, individual study and actual execution separate.

reviews.reason: No existing function slows spoilage. A small air-drying tray for crushed safe roots is a feasible precursor that requires actual materials and suitable weather. Its effectiveness must depend on measured moisture and exposure, not a preservation label. The two carried roots remain ordinary roots until processing actually occurs. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: A completed tray or drying label is not itself pleasure or sustained satisfaction. The measurable benefit is slower subsequent decay while the food remains sufficiently dry. Actual consumption may receive the same canonical meal-experience food-enjoyment rule specified for preparation: actual eater, at least 8 accepted nutrition in a 10-round window, safe nonspoiled intake and positive appetite; 0.4 pleasure, cap 0.8, duration 4, refresh only, 10-round shared food cooldown and one grant per intake window. It is not an additional preserved-food reward. No maintained satisfaction is inferred from unattended storage. A real comparison establishing previously unconfirmed spoilage behavior can qualify through probe and the existing information-confirmed source, subject to that source's novelty, cap and cooldown rules.
reviews.visualReview: Render the acquired stones and bark as a small ground tray with only the food actually loaded. Show paid setup/crushing progress, moisture, drying or rain-paused status, accumulated spoilage and current decay multiplier. Bind shrinking food mass and rewetting to food-drying-progress and food-rewetted; completion changes appearance only when the moisture threshold is reached. Replay water transfers and actual material placement, and clearly distinguish predicted drying work from completed preserved food.
reviews.specification: Implement root-air-drying-v1. Public schema: {operation:'build'|'load'|'unload'|'dismantle', processId?, trayId?, inputStackId?, quantity?, stoneIds?, barkId?, x?, y?}. Use the same shared reference, coordinate, mass and process contracts as root preparation. Independently implement drying; record reuse of its crushing, food-provenance and escrow code as code reuse, not functional equivalence or personal mastery. Build requires two actual stone units and one bark unit, accessible ground and a living trained actor. Reserve these materials; two active rounds at 1 energy each assemble a non-solid radius-0.4 tray, capacity two root units, with 0.65 interaction reach. Validate shared placement against obstacles and incompatible work footprints. Materials remain conserved components and cannot simultaneously serve another process. Loading requires owned unspoiled meadow roots; crush on the tray using a support stone for two active rounds per root at 1 energy per round. Record all original food composition, harvest and decay history. Root wet mass starts from its actual resource composition: water 50%, other mass 50%; nutrition remains 14 per original root, toxicity zero. After loading, drying is passive, with explicit remaining water-removal work. At each dt=1, when uncovered, not raining and temperature is between 10 and 40 C, remove at most 0.005 mass units of water per root and never below a water fraction of 0.12; transfer removed water to the environmental water ledger. At other temperatures pause drying. Rain adds actual environmental water at up to 0.01 mass per root per round, bounded by the original 50% water fraction. Resolve temperature, rain, cover and exposure from shared weather and geometry, not applicant labels; add a conservative explicit weather-state field if necessary rather than assume favorable conditions. Before dry completion, use crushed-food decay at 1.25 times baseline; at water fraction <=0.12 use 0.35 times baseline while actually dry. Rewetting above 0.12 immediately removes that benefit. Never reset accumulated spoilage, reverse spoiled food, remove toxins or increase nutrients. Completion emits a dried composite food stack retained in the tray; unload transfers that actual stack to inventory. Away from the tray, continue tracking moisture, rain exposure, decay and provenance; no automatic waterproof container. Existing eat consumes its real composition. Owner, component identities, escrow, work progress, moisture, environmental transfers and decay persist. Pause active work on lost reach or energy. Any multi-round actor operation cancels on death, leaving uniquely owned materials and the actual partly processed food at the tray; passive exposure remains physical state, not a dead actor's continuing action. Manual cancellation follows the same rule, without refunds or duplication. Dismantling takes one round and 1 energy, returns actual components at their current condition and deposits any food unchanged. Declare drying-tray-built, food-drying-progress, food-drying-completed and food-rewetted, plus process-progress/process-completed/process-stopped for active work. Dependencies include shared weather/geometry, food water-mass accounting, decay, eat and process ownership; implement within this handoff. Existing foods retain their original decay history; migrate root water composition without changing mass or nutrition. No stock, tray or mastery is supplied by development.

reviews.reason: The implemented process already provides the requested physical effect: weather-dependent drying of actual roots, with reduced spoilage while sufficiently dry and conserved food composition and accumulated age. Crushing alone does not preserve food. No equipment or materials are supplied by reuse. The current inventory contains three roots with decay 6.91485786, rather than the older reported value; eligibility and processing must use live state. Individual learning is required.
reviews.experienceReview: Physical benefit is delayed food loss, not healing or immediate happiness. Actual consumption continues to use real nutrition and toxicity and existing meal rules. Personally testing preservation may qualify for the existing grounded-understanding source through probe's information-confirmed event only when a real experiment establishes new information: amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8, refresh cooldown 12; maintained gain 0.035 and decay 0.0015 under the registered qualification rule. Reobserving the same fact does not qualify. Paid completed practice may use the existing root-air-drying practice-confirmed rule only for its qualified changed-output milestones: amount 0.4, cap 0.5, duration 8, refresh cooldown 12; maintained gain 0.02, decay 0.001. These are existing sources, not additional alias rewards. Requesting, studying, mastery and merely owning reserves award nothing.
reviews.visualReview: Reuse the tray, actual loaded-root and moisture/progress presentation, including wetting and spoilage state. Bind replay and subscriptions to drying-tray-built, food-drying-progress, food-drying-completed, food-rewetted, process-inspected and the existing process lifecycle events. Show actual paid construction and processing, not a completed tray or preserved food before execution. Placement and interaction remain tied to the registered shared geometry.
reviews.specification: Reuse the existing root-air-drying public schema and executable contract unchanged. Learning takes four rounds; review itself advances no time. Build requires two actual stone units and one bark, with two work rounds costing one energy each. A tray accepts at most two original root units; raw roots require two crushing rounds per root at one energy per round. Thus the current three-root stack cannot all occupy one tray simultaneously. Use actual ownership, reachable placement, shared geometry, equipment availability and weather checks. Drying at 10–40 C in uncovered dry weather removes at most 0.005 water mass per original root per round toward water fraction 0.12; rain can restore up to 0.01 per root per round, bounded by original water content. Apply the existing moisture-dependent spoilage rule, never reset age, invent nutrients or remove toxicity. Retain the existing progress, remaining-work, provenance, escrow and cancellation contracts; actor work cancels on death without duplicating or deleting reserved property, while unattended material follows the existing physical-process rules. No new interface, duplicate implementation, satisfaction source or migration is needed.

reviews.reason: The requested root-preservation function is already implemented by root-air-drying. It supplies a feasible precursor—constructing and loading a real drying tray—and a measurable weather-dependent preservation effect without assuming equipment, supplies or mastery. Current owned state shows two roots with decay 11.50346239, not the request's earlier three-root count and decay. Only the actual remaining owned food can be processed.
reviews.experienceReview: Successful preservation can retain usable nutrition, but does not itself heal or automatically produce happiness. Eating remains governed by real composition and existing meal rules. A personally performed experiment that establishes a new preservation fact can emit qualified information-confirmed through probe and use grounded-understanding: amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8, refresh cooldown 12, maintained gain 0.035 and decay 0.0015. Qualified paid practice milestones with actual changed outputs may use the already registered root-air-drying practice-confirmed source: amount 0.4, cap 0.5, duration 8, refresh cooldown 12, maintained gain 0.02 and decay 0.001. Qualification and continued maintenance follow those existing executable rules; repeated facts, learning and mastery do not qualify. Do not add a second preservation satisfaction source under this request's name.
reviews.visualReview: Use the existing physical tray and food-state rendering, showing actual loads, moisture, weather exposure, remaining work and accumulated spoilage. Declare existing subscriptions drying-tray-built, food-drying-progress, food-drying-completed, food-rewetted, process-inspected and process lifecycle events for observable progress and replay. Neither meeting-location labels nor the review should display equipment or finished preserved food that does not exist.
reviews.specification: Reuse the existing root-air-drying interface, schema and physical-process contract unchanged; four rounds of personal learning are required. Constructing a tray consumes/reserves the contract's two actual stone units and one bark through two work rounds at one energy per round. Load no more than two original root units; each raw root requires two crushing rounds at one energy per round. Validate current inventory, actual material access, interaction reach, unobstructed shared placement and weather rather than treating the meeting location as equipment. Under the existing contract, uncovered dry weather at 10–40 C removes at most 0.005 water mass per original root per round toward water fraction 0.12; rain restores up to 0.01 per root per round, capped by original water. Preserve nutrition, toxicity, input provenance and accumulated spoilage, and apply only the existing moisture-dependent preservation effect. reviews.reason: The implemented stone-and-bark root preparation already provides a feasible version of the requested function: mechanically prepare owned roots with measurable changes and explicit costs. The three owned roots are suitable inputs, subject to their actual remaining freshness. Stone and bark must be obtained and validated; neither equipment nor mastery is supplied by this review. Cooking, detoxification and preservation are not necessary for these roots, whose recorded toxicity is zero, and are not effects of this method.
reviews.experienceReview: Physical benefit comes from subsequently consuming the food's conserved nutrition, not from preparation itself; no extra calories, health or comfort are awarded. Do not add an alias satisfaction source. Retain the existing root-preparation practice rule only for qualified, paid, completed practice with genuinely changed outputs and a limited confirmed milestone—not requesting, study, mastery or every routine batch. Subscribe to practice-confirmed on root-preparation: the performing actor receives amount 0.4, cap 0.5, duration 8, refresh repetition and cooldown 12; maintained gain is 0.02 per qualifying event with decay 0.001. Actual eating emits meal-experience and uses the established meal feedback rules without inventing preparation enjoyment or label-only dietary diversity. Genuine experiments confirming new information may use the existing information-confirmed rule through probe, never an additional duplicate reward.
reviews.visualReview: Use the existing preparation presentation: display the actual reserved stone and bark, root quantity, working progress and resulting crushed food at the real work location. Bind food-preparation-started and food-preparation-completed to successful state transitions, and process-stopped to cancellation. Replay must represent paid work, retained partial processing and released implements faithfully; do not display cooking, steam, a constructed kitchen, extra food or a safety certification. Any wellbeing display must follow an actual qualified experience event, not learning or completion alone.
reviews.specification: Reuse root-preparation unchanged; individual learning requires 2 simulation rounds. Its public contract governs input references, quantities, progress and cancellation. Reserve one actual reusable stone and one actual reusable bark; process 1–4 owned roots at two working rounds per raw root and one energy per working round. Validate ownership, implement availability, interaction reach and the actual work location against shared geometry. Preserve input provenance, mass, nutrients, toxicity and accumulated spoilage rather than using the crushed-root resource's nominal zero nutrition as the meal's composition. Completed crushed roots age at 1.25 baseline: preparation is not preservation, sterilization or detoxification. Eating remains a separate eat operation, with actual nutrition, toxicity and spoilage checks; food does not directly heal. Track actual remaining work and partially processed food. Cancellation, including death, must release reserved implements and retain the actual food, processing fraction and age under the existing ownership/death rules, without duplicating or deleting escrow. No berries, heat source, vessel or new recipe is required for this equivalent method. Implementation and review advance no simulation time and grant no mastery.

reviews.reason: Gathering transfers existing exposed stock; it does not assess or separate bark. Root preparation consumes no new tree material and cannot supply its own implements. A small bark-assessment and separation capability is therefore missing. The observed tree currently exposes branch stock, not a demonstrated bark reserve: neither its name nor inspection alone may create bark. Development can provide assessment and a material-conserving branch-peeling precursor without assuming successful extraction or supplying tools. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: Inspection, requesting, learning and obtaining a label award nothing. Paid assessment or separation that genuinely establishes previously unknown, personally observed material behavior may emit information-confirmed through the existing probe-equivalent qualification logic, with evidence and qualified=true only for new verified information. Reuse grounded-understanding, not a second bark-specific source: the observing actor receives amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition and cooldown 12; qualified continued experiments contribute the existing maintained gain 0.035 with decay 0.0015. Repeating an established fact does not qualify. Ordinary repetitive peeling provides no automatic pleasure or maintained satisfaction: it is effortful material acquisition, and useful output alone does not demonstrate enjoyment. Health, hunger, fatigue and protected mental accounts remain independent.
reviews.visualReview: Show assessment uncertainty and explicit material/tool failures, not a successful bark icon before extraction. Bind process visuals to the declared start, progress, completion and stop events: display the real branch, diminishing outer layer, separated bark quantity, residual core, tool reservation and remaining paid work. Replay must reconstruct conserved input/output amounts and cancellations from those events. Use actual ground-stack positions and existing shared collision/interaction rules; a work marker is non-solid and supplies no shelter, comfort or invented room effects. Leave the observed standing tree visually unchanged when only an already gathered branch is peeled.
reviews.specification: Implement bark-extraction@1 with public arguments {action: assess|peel|inspect|cancel, targetId, toolId?, quantity?: positive number, processId?}. Shared references use persistent actor, object, stack and process IDs, world coordinates, dt, existing interaction distance and shared collision geometry. Individual learning is required. Reuse gather's stock-transfer and root-preparation's reservation/progress code separately from this new function; neither code reuse grants those abilities or changes their contracts. Dependencies: actual branch/material composition, ownership, tool hardness/contact geometry, inventory capacity, source stock, persistent process and event systems. Assess costs one round and 0.2 energy, requires visible target within its actual interaction boundary, and reports retained physical facts, uncertainty, required tool and estimated recoverable mass. It does not extract material. Inspect full retained tree/material state before migration: preserve all known composition and source history. An unknown standing trunk receives no invented bark reserve and remains ineligible for trunk stripping. Minimal executable precursor: gather an actual exposed branch through the existing gather interface, then peel that owned branch. Introduce a conservative layered model for otherwise composition-unspecified branch material: at most 10% of its existing mass is separable outer bark, with the remainder woody core; partition existing mass, fuel and provenance rather than adding biomass, and record this explicit model assumption. Known contradictory composition overrides this default. Never apply the model to previously separated material or replenish peeled fractions. A standard 1.1-mass branch can thus yield at most 0.11 mass, or 0.366666 bark units at the existing 0.3 mass/unit; do not round upward or claim this meets root-preparation's one-unit requirement. Peeling requires an owned actual stone or flint implement with hardness at least 8 and a usable contact edge confirmed by assessment; absent prerequisites yield an actionable failure, not supplied items. For each original branch unit, require two work-rounds at one energy each, linearly scaled for fractional quantities. Reserve selected branch material and the reusable tool atomically in actor-owned process escrow; retain ownership and prevent simultaneous use. Each paid work increment separates the proportional bark mass and updates remaining layer mass, woody-core mass, actual work remaining and provenance. Preserve total material mass and partition chemical fuel without duplication; do not let stripped core re-enter the unmodified branch recipe or regenerate bark. Outputs retain source IDs, processing history and age; no nutrition or toxicity is erased by relabeling. Completion requires all declared paid work and transfers only actual separated bark and residual core to available inventory capacity, otherwise leaving owned outputs at the work location. Progress requires a living actor, sufficient energy, access to escrow and continued interaction range. Loss of access or energy pauses; cancellation or death terminates work, releases the tool, and leaves completed bark plus partially peeled material with their actual remaining work and ownership at the process location. No escrow is cloned, deleted or reset by death or respawn. Do not modify standing-tree health or geometry during this precursor; future trunk removal requires separately represented finite tissue and wound effects. Declare bark-assessed, bark-peeling-started, bark-peeling-progress, bark-peeling-completed and bark-peeling-stopped events, with process/source/output IDs, paid energy, transferred mass, progress and failure reason; retain existing information-confirmed validation. No time passes during implementation.

Actual branch acquisition uses existing gather with source depletion and its own effort cost. Validate ownership, inspected tool suitability and actual interaction reach against shared geometry. args.function: Provide a feasible physical method for investigating an owned unfamiliar plant-food sample's food suitability, including nutrition, toxicity or preparation requirements only to the extent actual tests can establish them. Distinguish measured results from unresolved safety uncertainty.
args.conditions: I own one hazelnut sample, item-32-ash-4-785. Observing it at tick 40 revealed only visible state, not nutrition or toxicity. I have not eaten it. Health is 100, satiety 57.1, energy 39.8; two known-safe roots remain available. No testing equipment or relevant mastery is established.

reviews.reason: The implemented probe already supports non-ingestive physical testing of a small owned material sample, rather than observation alone. This provides the feasible initial investigation requested. It does not establish nutritional value, absence of toxins or a safe preparation method merely from appearance or resource identity. No equivalent analytical assay or equipment is established, so those questions must remain unresolved unless actual supported measurements answer them.
reviews.experienceReview: A successful physical trial that establishes genuinely new observed information can use the existing grounded-understanding source through probe's declared information-confirmed event with qualified=true. The participant is the testing actor; an unsuccessful trial or another observation of an already known fact does not qualify. Existing temporary feedback is 0.8, cap 1, held for 8 rounds, refreshed by qualifying events subject to a 12-round cooldown. Existing maintained feedback gains 0.035 from qualifying continued investigation and decays at 0.0015 under the registered rule. Reuse that equivalence without adding another source. Requesting, consulting, learning, merely consuming the test fraction and calling the sample safe award nothing; health and nutrition remain independent.
reviews.visualReview: Reuse probe's trial-result and trial-material-consumed events, plus information-confirmed only when justified, for subscription validation and replay. Show the actual sample reference, paid effort, removed sample quantity, performed test, measured result and explicitly unresolved food-safety questions. Preserve the remaining stack's real quantity and provenance. Do not display a safety badge, inferred nutrient values or fabricated laboratory apparatus; there is no new geometry, collision shape or environmental effect.
reviews.specification: Use probe's existing physical-trial operation with the explicit owned reference item-32-ash-4-785, not another visible-state observation. Retain the existing public schema and shared reference resolver; consult its full contract to select the supported physical test rather than inventing an assay parameter. Validate ownership and at least 0.1 sample unit before execution. Cost: one simulation round, 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual sample unit; no ingestion, animal testing, extra equipment or automatic consumption of the remaining food. Record the performed method, consumed fraction, provenance, directly measured results and limitations in personal evidence. Only physical properties actually tested may become findings; compositional nutrition, toxicological safety and necessary preparation remain unknown without a suitable measurement. A destructive physical sample test may provide preparation-relevant evidence but cannot certify edibility. Use existing atomic probe completion and failure semantics, with no background process or duplicated sample. This reuses implemented behavior and code, not a new function; implementation review advances no time and grants no mastery or stock.

Its prerequisites, costs and conserved outputs match this request. The observed object represents fallen branch stock, not harvestable standing-tree tissue. Its two branch units are not owned bark, and neither a suitable tool nor successful assessment is established. Individual learning is required.
reviews.experienceReview: Reuse the existing practice:bark-extraction source, not an alias. A successful paid completion emitting practice-confirmed with qualified=true may grant the participating actor 0.4 temporary satisfaction, capped at 0.5 for eight rounds, refreshing with a 12-round cooldown. Qualification requires the existing limited genuine progress milestone with changed physical outputs; application, learning, mastery and routine output alone do not qualify. Its maintained component gains 0.02 on qualifying participation and decays 0.001 per round under the registered rule. A genuinely new experimentally confirmed finding may separately use information-confirmed through probe under grounded-understanding's existing qualification and cooldown rules; a repeated observation does not qualify. Bark possession itself grants no comfort, health or nutritional benefit.
reviews.visualReview: Reuse bark-assessed, bark-peeling-started, bark-peeling-progress, bark-peeling-completed and bark-peeling-stopped for subscription and replay. Show actual eligibility findings, inspected contact, paid progress, remaining work, separated bark/fines and changed core mass. Source stock changes only on actual transfer; do not depict trunk wounds or tree injury when only represented fallen branches were collected. Show unavailable inputs and failed reach checks without presenting successful extraction.
reviews.specification: Reuse the existing bark-extraction contract unchanged, including its public assessment/peeling parameters, source validation, progress and cancellation behavior. Assessment costs one round and 0.2 energy; peeling requires actual eligible material and a personally inspected reusable stone or flint, with two active work-round equivalents and two energy per original intact branch unit, reduced for fractional or already processed material. Use existing gather for exposed branch-stock transfer, charging its actual costs and depletion; do not strip the source object's standing trunk or infer represented living tissue from its kind label. An unspecified intact branch may partition at most 10% of its existing mass into outer bark, with whole tenth-unit bark outputs rounded down and residual mass retained as bark-fines. Preserve core, fines, provenance and remaining work. Enforce shared reach and collision geometry; never teleport inputs. Multi-round work must stop on death, retaining partial processing and returning or grounding actual escrow exactly once under the existing ownership contract. No stock, tool or mastery is granted by review.

The nearby object exposes nine units of fallen branches; that establishes source stock, not owned or already assessed bark. The two owned stones are possible reusable contacts, but a personally inspected suitable contact and eligible material must still be validated. Root-air-drying mastery does not confer bark-extraction mastery.

reviews.reason: The implemented probe interface already supports non-ingestive physical testing of a small owned sample, separately from direct visual observation. Reuse it for the feasible preliminary investigation; no supplied capability or equipment establishes nutrition, toxicity or general food safety. A physical trial must report its actual observations and leave unsupported food-safety questions unresolved. Neither tasting nor feeding another participant is required or authorized.
reviews.experienceReview: Application, study and an inconclusive attempt earn no feedback. If the performed trial actually confirms previously unresolved information, emit information-confirmed through probe with qualified=true and the actor as the sole beneficiary, using the existing grounded-understanding source—not a new alias. Its temporary feedback is 0.8, capped at 1, held for 8 rounds, refresh repetition and 12-round cooldown. Its maintained component gains 0.035 only on qualifying confirmation events and decays by 0.0015 under the existing rule. Repeated confirmation of the same fact does not qualify. Mechanical information can qualify as understanding without implying food safety; unsupported conclusions cannot. No separate pleasure, physical-comfort or health benefit is established by testing.
reviews.visualReview: Show the actual sample targeted, the performed trial, paid sample and energy costs, observed result, and remaining quantity in the existing probe event presentation and replay. Clearly distinguish measured observations from unresolved nutrition and toxicity. Do not display a safe-food badge, invented laboratory equipment or an eating animation. Any consumed fragment must disappear only through the recorded material debit; the remainder retains its actual world or inventory representation.
reviews.specification: Use probe's existing physical-trial operation with the explicit owned sample item-32-ash-4-785. Validate current ownership, remaining quantity and the chosen supported trial before charging anything. Cost: one simulation round, 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual sample unit, as already implemented. Select only an executable non-ingestive material trial supported by probe; declare its method and any required actual implements before execution. If an implement is required but unavailable, fail without inventing equipment or results. Record the tested quantity, method, conditions, consumed sample provenance and observed result. A mechanical response or visible interior, if actually exposed by the supported trial, establishes only that observation—not nutrient content, absence of toxins or suitability for eating. If probe has no supported trial relevant beyond the existing observation, return that limitation without pretending to perform a food assay. Preserve the untested remainder, ownership and accumulated spoilage; do not convert testing into consumption or change nutrition, toxicity, health or hunger. Use the existing probe public schema and trial-result/trial-material-consumed events; retain existing atomic completion and failure behavior, with no new persistent process, escrow, objects or collision geometry. Implementation, individual learning and execution remain separate; this review advances no simulation time.

Its existing maintained component gains 0.035 per qualifying event and decays 0.0015 per round, within existing bounds. Repeating an already established fact, requesting, learning, or merely describing uncertainty earns nothing. There is no eating pleasure, nutritional benefit or health improvement from this non-ingestive procedure.
reviews.visualReview: Present the actual observation or trial at the actor's location, with the referenced sample, any genuinely used tools, the paid sample loss and the measured result visible in the event record and replay. Preserve the remainder's composition, age and provenance, and explicitly leave nutrition, toxicity and untested hazards unknown. No ingestion, animal exposure, free equipment, food transformation or safety certification is implied. Use existing trial-result, trial-material-consumed and information-confirmed events. This is a one-round operation, not a persistent process: commit sample consumption and results atomically only for executed work; death before execution cancels without consuming or duplicating material. Source acquisition remains the separate existing gather operation and depletes actual branch stock. Standing trunks without represented tissue remain ineligible. Emit trial-result for a completed examination and information-confirmed only when actual evidence establishes a previously unresolved, personally new observable fact; qualified=true must reference that evidence and must not mean that food safety has been established. The participant is the examining actor. Apply the registered 0.8 amount, cap 1, eight-round hold, refresh repetition and 12-round cooldown; maintained satisfaction uses the existing 0.035 gain and 0.0015 decay under its registered qualification and cooldown semantics. Reinspection of the same fact, successful reference resolution alone, requesting and learning earn nothing. There is no separate pleasure award: the supported benefit here is resolving real uncertainty, not an established enjoyable sensory experience. Health, hunger and protected mental accounts remain unchanged except for ordinary simulation costs.
reviews.visualReview: Bind replay and presentation to existing trial-result, trial-material-consumed, information-confirmed and failed events. Show the actual sample identity, examination action, paid energy, any genuinely consumed fraction, measured observations and explicitly unresolved safety questions. Observation leaves inventory quantity unchanged. Render material changes only when a paid trial actually changes the sample; use authoritative item state and location, with no spawned equipment, safety badge or invented analytical visualization.

Accept target='item:item-48-cedar-4-1203' through the shared item-reference resolver; resolve the persistent item ID against authoritative current state, validate ownership and remaining quantity, and preserve origin and history. An owned inventory item is accessible without requiring a ground-object observation entry; ground items still require actual visibility and interaction distance under shared geometry. Never substitute a resource prototype, invent a sample or silently choose another item. Public schema: probe({target:string, mode:'observe'|'trial', test?:string}); retain compatible existing parameters. For mode='observe', perform one round of non-ingestive external examination at 0.2 energy, consuming no material. Report only physically observable represented features, current observable deterioration and observation limits; provenance may be reported as retained records, not as a newly measured fact. Do not reveal hidden nutrition or toxicity fields as analytical results. A valid owned reference must not fail merely because it is absent from observedObjectIds. Trial mode retains the existing one-round, 0.5-energy, 0.1-unit cost, but must validate an explicit executable physical test, actual required implements and exposure constraints before reserving or consuming anything; no ingestion, hazardous exposure, imaginary assay or unsupported safety certification. External inspection is the immediately executable precursor. Commit observation or trial effects once, with an idempotent operation ID; record actual cost, consumed quantity, findings, unresolved questions and evidence IDs in personal knowledge. Failed validation costs no material. No persistent work or escrow is needed for the one-round inspection; death before execution cancels it without effects. Any existing trial implementation spanning rounds must retain actual remaining work, pause safely and cancel on death, releasing unconsumed actor-owned escrow once while preserving consumed material and completed changes. reviews.experienceReview: Reuse grounded-understanding rather than register a duplicate source. A completed observation or physical trial may emit information-confirmed with qualified=true only when it establishes genuinely new, method-supported information for the investigating actor. Mere target resolution, application, studying, failed trials and repeated known facts do not qualify. Use the existing temporary rule: amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition with a 12-round cooldown. Use its existing maintained rule: gain 0.035 per qualifying event and decay 0.0015 per round, under the registered bounded source saturation and global mental cap. No separate pleasure source is needed for sample handling itself. Unknown food safety remains unknown; neither feedback nor investigation changes nutrition, health or survival accounts.
reviews.visualReview: Show the resolved inventory sample and quantity, observation versus destructive-trial mode, disclosed costs, confirmation requirement and actual result. Bind result presentation to trial-result, material loss to trial-material-consumed, and qualified discovery feedback to information-confirmed. Replay must identify the real target, paid effort, consumed fraction and evidence limits. Do not depict ingestion, invented laboratory equipment, successful shell opening without an actual result, or a food-safety approval badge. Inventory inspection creates no world obstacle or duplicate sample.
reviews.specification: Hand off a versioned correction to probe, preserving its interface ID, existing mastery, costs and evidence history. Public parameters: target (exact object/item ID or resource:ID), mode (observe|trial), method, and confirmDestructive (default false). Resolve exact owned inventory IDs against authoritative inventory before spatial-object lookup; inventory items need no separate world-object registration. resource:ID must select an actual eligible stack and report its resolved ID; ambiguous selections require clarification. Never substitute another item for an unavailable exact ID. External subjects require visibility and actual interaction reach of 0.65 using shared geometry; inventory subjects are accessible to their owner. Before destructive execution, disclose the method, one-round duration, 0.5 energy cost, 0.1-unit sample consumption, required implements and modeled hazards; require explicit confirmation. Observation takes one round and 0.2 energy without consuming material. Support direct visual inspection and feasible manual physical trials using existing probe mechanics; validate method-specific requirements, and explain unavailable measurements rather than inventing results. No tool, assay, heat source or safety knowledge is supplied. An actual qualifying assessment experiment may emit information-confirmed through bark-extraction and activate grounded-understanding only when it establishes new verified information: amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8, refresh repetition and cooldown 12; maintained gain 0.035 with decay 0.0015 under the registered rule. Existing probe supports observation and small physical trials, but does not provide a food-composition assay or a persistent opened sample for subsequent examination. Develop a minimal non-ingestive opening and inspection precursor, not an unsupported safety detector. It can establish mechanical accessibility and visible condition; it cannot establish nutritional value, absence of toxins, or suitability for eating. Neither the food's name nor its hidden resource values constitute experimental evidence. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: Temporary pleasure is not inferred from handling food or from making the request. Successful experimentation can provide bounded understanding: bind this interface's information-confirmed event to the existing grounded-understanding source, not a new alias. The participant is the actor who actually performed the paid experiment; qualified=true requires a genuinely new, personally unconfirmed observation supported by completed work and retained evidence. Use the existing amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition and 12-round cooldown. Maintained satisfaction uses that same source's gain 0.035 per qualified event and decay 0.0015 per round, bounded by its existing saturation; no continuing gain without further qualifying participation. Reopening an already established equivalent result, learning, labels and inspection of unchanged evidence do not qualify. Nutrition, health and survival remain independent.
reviews.visualReview: Show the actual sample and reusable tool at the shared work position, with a contact/compression animation only during paid work. Bind progress and remaining-work displays to food-inspection-progress; completion shows an opened/fractured sample, and cancellation shows the actual partial state and released items. Retain event-linked replay records for material reservation, energy spent, progress, release and findings. Display measured or observed fields separately from unknown nutrition and toxicity, with an explicit 'not a safety test' notice. Do not display a safe-food badge, invented laboratory equipment, or an unperformed eating animation.
reviews.specification: Implement non-ingestive-food-inspection@1. Public schema: {action:'start'|'continue'|'inspect'|'cancel', sampleId, toolId?, processId?}; shared references use persistent actor/item/process IDs, world coordinates, dt=1 and interaction reach 0.65. Require individual mastery, a living actor, an owned hazelnut quantity of at least 0.1 unit, and, for opening, an actual reusable stone or flint with sufficient hardness. No tools or stock are supplied. Depend on existing inventory, material hardness, observation, provenance, event and process systems; record code reuse separately from this new functional contract. Implement the missing minimal fracture mechanism: two active work rounds, each costing 0.5 energy, apply hard-tool compression to one reserved 0.1-unit portion and expose its interior. This is not a chemical test. Validate tool contact and an accessible, non-overlapping working position against shared collision geometry each round. Reserve sample and tool in an actor-owned process escrow; record original lot, age, composition, mass, completed work and remaining work. Progress requires presence, available energy and valid contact; absence pauses without progress while ordinary aging continues. Death or explicit cancellation stops the process and releases the tool and actual partly worked sample at the work location, preserving ownership/provenance under ordinary inventory rules; never clone, erase or reset escrow. Completion releases the unchanged-mass opened sample and reusable tool. Retain fragments as one provenance-linked lot rather than inventing edible-kernel yields. Opening neither creates nutrients nor removes toxicity; preserve actual composition and accumulated spoilage, and apply the existing exposed/crushed-food aging mechanism only if its physical applicability is validated, otherwise retain baseline aging and report that limitation. Inspection costs one round and 0.2 energy and requires the sample in reach. Return only represented observable features, exposure/fracture state and existing gross spoilage indicators, with unknown fields explicitly null. Never expose nutrition/toxicity metadata as a measurement, interpret lack of visible spoilage as safety, or invent unrepresented anatomy. A successful paid opening may confirm the new fact that this sample's interior became mechanically accessible; it cannot confirm food safety. Declare food-inspection-started, food-inspection-progress, food-inspection-completed and food-inspection-stopped events, plus existing trial-result and information-confirmed. Results include evidence IDs, method, sample provenance, actual costs, limitations and remaining work. Migration adds optional inspection/process fields to existing lots without changing their contents, age or ownership. No passive processing, ingestion, remote interaction, new actors or automatic future actions. Implementation and study advance no simulation time during review.

Reuse therefore provides the requested feasible acquisition mechanism, not a promise of sufficient local yield.
reviews.experienceReview: Successful paid peeling can provide limited grounded capability-progress feedback through the existing bark-extraction practice-confirmed rule when its qualification predicate is actually satisfied: performer only, amount 0.4, cap 0.5, hold duration 8 rounds, refresh with 12-round cooldown. Its maintained component gains 0.02 on qualifying events and decays 0.001 per round; mastery or routine unqualified repetition awards nothing. A genuinely new experimentally confirmed fact may separately trigger the existing information-confirmed grounded-understanding rule: qualified performer, amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8, refresh cooldown 12, maintained gain 0.035 and decay 0.0015. Do not duplicate either functional source under a bark-acquisition alias. Requesting, studying, receiving bark or naming an output grants no happiness; peeling itself provides no established nutrition, healing or physical comfort.
reviews.visualReview: Use existing bark-assessed, bark-peeling-started, bark-peeling-progress, bark-peeling-completed and bark-peeling-stopped event bindings. Show actual assessed suitability, paid work progress, exposed core, separated bark/fines, tool location and retained partial work at the shared worksite. Replay must distinguish gathered branch stock from peeling outputs and show real source depletion; never depict trunk stripping, a full bark unit or a completed tray unless actual state supports it. Subscribe to practice-confirmed and information-confirmed only for validated existing experience feedback.
reviews.specification: Reuse the existing bark-extraction contract unchanged; consult its full schema before individual study and execution. Learning requires two simulation rounds and does not occur during review. Assess the actual source/material and personally inspect the reusable stone contact; ownership of two stones alone does not establish inspected suitability. Existing gather handles only genuinely exposed branch stock within shared interaction geometry, charging its normal costs and decrementing real stock; it does not fell or strip the tree. Peeling costs two active work-round equivalents and two energy per original branch unit, scaled to the actual remaining peelable fraction. Preserve material provenance and conserve bark, core and fines; whole-tenth bark units round down and residual mass remains fines. Never count proposed yield as inventory or as a completed drying tray. Use the existing public parameters, worksite reach/collision checks, escrow ownership, progress and completion rules. Interruption retains actual remaining work and partial materials; death cancels active work and leaves tools and partial material at the worksite without duplication or deletion. reviews.reason: The requested effect is conservative aggregation of compatible fractional supplies, not gathering, transfer, extraction or food processing. No supplied implemented interface provides it. Two validated 0.7-unit bark stacks can supply 1.0 unit and leave 0.4 units without producing material. Their full ownership, accessibility and compatibility must be checked at execution; the omitted second stack cannot be presumed invalid or available. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: This operation resolves a practical supply-addressing obstruction but ordinary stack handling is not, by itself, a pleasurable experience, a new experimentally confirmed finding or sustained meaningful participation. Assign no automatic temporary pleasure or maintained satisfaction for combining, requesting, learning or enabling a later craft. Do not award existing practice sources under an aggregation alias. Any later qualifying performed experience is evaluated by its own registered rules, with health, nutrition and physical comfort remaining independent.
reviews.visualReview: Show selected reachable stacks and their quantities before commitment, a one-round handling/progress indicator, and the actual resulting combined supply with expandable component provenance. On success show 1.4 bark units only if validated quantities total fourteen tenths; later reservation should visibly show 1.0 transferred and 0.4 remaining. Replay the declared operation events with actual locations, paid energy, ledger changes and cancellation state. Do not show a completed tray, improved material quality or a happiness effect merely from combining.
reviews.specification:
Implement material-stack-combine@1 with interface material-stack-combine. Public schema: {operation:'combine', sourceIds:string[2..16], expectedVersions?:object}; return {status, outputId, quantityTenths, componentLots, costs, failureReason}. Shared references use existing actor/item IDs, resource IDs, world coordinates, interaction reach 0.65, dt=1 and integer quantityTenths. Requires individual mastery, a living actor, at least two distinct unlocked owned stacks, sufficient energy, and actual accessible material. Carried items are accessible; owned ground items must each be within interaction reach with unobstructed contact. Ownership alone does not imply proximity. No tool or additional material is required.
Compatibility: use the same canonical resource and unit definition, with actual material form and intrinsic properties satisfying the same downstream requirements. Compare represented processing profiles, not names alone. Reject incompatible solid/fines forms, incompatible physical processing states, or different intrinsic unit masses; never convert bark-fines into bark. Different origins and histories are allowed but remain separate component lots. Resolve the two named bark stacks from full retained state before deciding compatibility.
State: each combined item has an ordinary addressable item ID and a component-lot ledger preserving original IDs, quantity, mass, composition, fuel, moisture, age, decay, toxicity, provenance and processing history. Flatten nested ledgers without duplicating lots. Conserve all quantities and extensive properties; retain heterogeneous properties per lot rather than replacing them with an improved average. A combined supply remains subject to its actual component aging and spoilage.
Execution: one active simulation round at 0.5 energy for this bounded operation. Validate and lock source versions at start, reserve them in owner-attributed transaction escrow, and track remainingWork=1. At completion revalidate life, reach, ownership, energy and compatibility; debit energy once and atomically replace source records with one combined record at the actor's accessible location, without changing carried versus ground status or teleporting material. Require all sources to have the same carried/ground disposition; ground sources must be reachable at the chosen output point. Output placement uses shared collision and placement checks, creates no room or blocking structure, and preserves carried load. Failure before commit changes no material. Cancellation, death or invalidation releases original source records at their actual locations with elapsed aging and any already-paid costs preserved; no escrow is cloned or deleted. Expose status and cancel operations and actual remaining work.
Integrate the composite representation with existing inventory and material-reservation consumers, including root-air-drying tray construction. A reservation of ten tenths from fourteen tenths selects stable component slices, transfers their exact mass and provenance into the constructed tray, and leaves four tenths with the corresponding histories. Count each slice only once; never treat a whole combined item as consumed when only part was requested. Preserve all existing tray eligibility, stone, work and energy requirements. Aggregation is not tray construction and creates no tray now.
Declare events material-combine-started, material-combine-completed and material-combine-stopped with actor, operation ID, source/output IDs, component quantities, work, costs and stop reason. Use existing process-progress only if its schema is satisfied. Dependencies are inventory ownership/locking, shared geometry, conservative material splitting and existing crafting reservations. Record code reuse separately from this new aggregation function. Migrate legacy stacks lazily to one-lot ledgers using their actual stored profiles and provenance; preserve IDs until successful commit and do not invent missing history. Implementation, study and use remain separate; review/development advances no simulation time.

reviews.reason: Existing root-preparation supplies the crushing operation, costs and food-accounting rules, but its fixed one-unit bark prerequisite cannot assess or use a physically sufficient fractional piece. Develop one shared fractional-surface extension for both applicants, reusing that implementation rather than creating another crushing function. The reported failure establishes a quantity restriction, not physical insufficiency. Ownership alone does not establish that the implements are currently reachable. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: A successful paid assessment or completed trial can confirm previously unknown surface suitability; application, study, a quantity-check failure and repeated known results cannot. Bind qualified information-confirmed events from root-preparation to the existing grounded-understanding source, not a new alias: participant is the actual assessor or experimenter, evidence must establish new personally unconfirmed information from the real inspected piece or trial. Retain amount 0.8, cap 1, hold duration 8, refresh repetition and cooldown 12; maintained gain 0.035 per qualifying event with decay 0.0015, sharing the existing source's bounded saturation and cooldown across interfaces. Crushing alone supplies no additional pleasure or maintained satisfaction, and mastery earns nothing. Existing practice rules may apply only under their existing qualification contract, without duplicate awards. Physical benefits remain actual later consumption and processing effects, not immediate comfort, healing or happiness.
reviews.visualReview: Show the actual sheet and stone at the validated work patch, with the selected root quantity and partial crushing state. Inspection displays usable dimensions, continuity, model-versus-measurement basis and the footprint test. Display remaining work, paid energy, reservation ownership and specific pause/failure conditions. Replay binds to the declared assessment, progress, completion and stop events, preserving source/output identities; it must never depict the unreserved second root as processed or fines as an assembled sheet.
reviews.specification: Implement root-preparation@2 with assess-surface and prepare-small operations, retaining the existing interface and legacy operations. Public schema: {operation, barkId, toolId, rootId?, quantity?:0.1..1 in actual supported increments, site?:{x,y}, processId?}; status/cancel require processId. Shared reference parameters: interaction reach 0.65, existing world collision rules, bark density default 500 kg/m3 and thickness 0.003 m only where unrepresented, one-root working footprint 0.16 by 0.16 m including containment margin. Existing measured geometry overrides defaults. Represent per-piece mass, dimensions, connectedness, holes, condition, source provenance, assessment evidence and model assumptions. A single extraction-derived bark lot may receive a mass-conserving rectangular-sheet fallback model with aspect ratio 1.5 during paid assessment, unless its retained history records fragmentation; preserve explicit uncertainty and distinguish model-derived dimensions from observations. Stack combining never joins sheets; fines are not a continuous surface. Do not multiply a per-unit profile by quantity twice: these 0.3 bark units normally represent 0.09 mass, subject to authoritative retained accounting. Assessment takes one round and 0.2 energy with the actual bark and stone accessible; check intact usable rectangle, flexibility, stone hardness at least 3, and a clear level support site. Report measured/modelled dimensions and exact unmet conditions; reserve no roots and grant no success merely from the supplied IDs. A suitable bark sheet contains food on firm ground; it is not a freestanding impact support. Preparation reserves only the selected usable sheet, reusable stone and at most one actual root; split the selected root quantity out of its stack and leave the other root untouched. Reuse root-preparation crushing behavior: two active work-round equivalents and two energy per root, preserving mass, nutrients, toxicity, age and provenance; resulting crushed material ages at 1.25 baseline and gains no nutrition, safety or preservation benefit. Each paid round requires a living actor, sufficient energy, reachable implements and an unobstructed work patch in shared geometry. Store owner, site, exact escrow IDs, workDone and workRemaining; progress changes only after paid work. Inaccessible conditions pause without work or energy debit while food ages; explicit cancellation and death terminate, releasing the same implements and the actual partially processed material at the site without cloning, deletion or work reset. Completion releases implements and the real output once, with idempotent event delivery. Declare root-surface-assessed and root-preparation-stopped; retain food-preparation-started, process-progress, food-preparation-completed and information-confirmed bindings. Event payloads include participant, source IDs, geometry basis, costs, progress, outputs and failure reasons. Migrate existing bark histories lazily without adding material or declaring them suitable; preserve active legacy processes and satisfaction equivalence keys. Reuse crushing, inventory, collision, provenance and feedback code explicitly; the new independently learnable content is surface assessment and fractional setup, requiring root-preparation mastery. Individual extension study is one round; implementation and review advance no simulation time.

reviews.reason: The same missing fractional-surface assessment affects this request. Existing probe can inspect and existing root-preparation can crush, but neither currently connects a physically sufficient fractional sheet to executable preparation. Use the single shared root-preparation@2 development above, not a second implementation. No root is required for assessment; preparing food later requires an actual owned root. Fines cannot substitute for a connected sheet merely by adding their mass. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: Use precisely the shared grounded-understanding subscription described for birch-3: qualified information-confirmed from an actual paid assessment or experiment, benefiting only its actual participant when it establishes personally new information. Amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8, refresh with cooldown 12; maintained gain 0.035 and decay 0.0015 under the existing shared source cap. Observing another actor's nominal-unit rejection does not establish this sheet's physical suitability. Rechecking a known finding, requesting, learning and labels earn nothing. There is no separate pleasure source for assessing bark or achieving mastery, and no automatic physical comfort, nutrition or food-safety effect.
reviews.visualReview: Use the shared surface-assessment and preparation presentation: highlight the actual selected sheet and stone, show connected usable dimensions and the required footprint, and mark assumptions separately from observations. Show fines as separate loose material, never a fabricated continuous surface. Bind observable costs, inspection results, pauses, remaining work and actual outputs to root-surface-assessed, process-progress, food-preparation-completed and root-preparation-stopped, with stable IDs for replay. Without an actual root and completed work, display no prepared food.
reviews.specification: Co-develop the identical root-preparation@2 contract specified for birch-3, including its public schema, shared physical parameters, conservative geometry model, event declarations, conserved escrow, progress/pause/completion/death-cancellation behavior, provenance and migration. Apply assess-surface to the explicitly selected bark and stone only after validating actual ownership, accessibility, physical profiles and a clear supporting site. Assessment costs one round and 0.2 energy and returns the usable connected rectangle, assumptions and exact sufficiency result. Do not consume the fines or manufacture an assembled sheet; this smallest version implements assessment and single-sheet preparation, not unsupported joining. If the sheet fails, report the missing dimensions or integrity rather than granting suitability. No root is reserved during assessment. prepare-small accepts an actual selected owned root quantity of at most one unit, costs two work-round equivalents and two energy per root, and otherwise uses the shared contract unchanged. Status exposes process owner, remaining work, escrow and geometry; cancellation or death leaves actual tools and partial food at the site exactly once. Reuse existing crushing and inspection infrastructure as code reuse, while recording fractional setup as the newly developed functionality. This applicant separately studies the extension for one round because root-preparation is already mastered; no mastery, materials, completed assessment or elapsed simulation time is supplied by development.
